title: LaCrosse Global Fund Services Agrees to Buy Bank of America Merrill Lynch's Global Alternative Fund
description: Officials from LaCrosse Global Fund Services announced Monday that the hedge fund service provider will purchase Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) Merrill Lynch's global alternative fund administration business and move its assets, which are between $5 billion and $6 billion, under administration assets to $21 billion.  The purchase amount is undisclosed and the transaction is subject to regulatory approval.  "The acquisition both complements and supplements our existing operations," commented LaCrosse's co-chief executive Christopher Kundro.  La Crosse's co-chief executive Stuart Feffer added, "In addition to bringing strong client relationships and a great team, this acquisition adds to our support capabilities for fund of funds and onshore European vehicles, including UCITS."  The purchase will also add two new office locations to LaCrosse's existing portfolio of nine, in New Jersey and Dublin.  SmarTrend currently has Bank of America in an Uptrend.  We are currently monitoring the stock's technicals and will alert subscribers to any change of trend direction.  Bank of America should find initial resistance at its 50-day moving average (MA) of $15.54 and further resistance at its 200-day MA of $16.23.  In the last five trading sessions, the 50-day MA has fallen 1.69% while the 200-day MA has slid 0.29%  Shares of Bank of America are trading down 3.65% Monday afternoon at $13.47.

Officials from La Crosse Global Fund Services announced Monday that the hedge fund service provider will purchase Bank of America Merrill Lynch's Global Alternative Fund administration business and move its assets of between $5 and $6 billion under administration assets to $21 billion. The purchase amount is undisclosed, and the transaction is subject to regulatory approval. Lacrosse's co-Chief Executive Christopher Cundro commented, saying, quote, "... the acquisition, both compliments and supplements, are existing operations." While Lacrosse's co-Chief Executive Stuart Pfeffer added, quote, "... in addition to bringing strong client relationships, and a great team, this acquisition adds to our support capabilities for fund of funds and onshore European vehicles including UCITS. The purchase will also add two new office locations, to LaCrosse's existing portfolio of 9 in New Jersey and Dublin. SmartTrend currently has Bank of America in an uptrend. We are currently monitoring the stock's technicals and will alert subscribers to any change of trend direction. Bank of America should find initial resistance at its 50-day moving average of $15.54, and further resistance at its 200-day at $16.23. In the last 5 trading sessions, the 50-day moving average has fallen almost 2%, while the 200-day has slid about a third of a percent. Shares of Bank of America are trading down almost 4 percent Monday afternoon at a price of $13.47 per share. I'm Christy Duffy for Smart Trend News.
